facts.statement: The IFSCA Banking Handbook has three components - General Directions (GEN), Conduct of Business Directions (COB) and Prudential Directions (PRU) - at versions GEN v5.0, COB v6.0 and PRU v5.0 as of April 2024.
An IFSC Banking Unit (IBU) is a branch of a Banking Company only - it cannot be set up as a standalone subsidiary.
facts.detail: IBC (subsidiary incorporated in IFSC) is the alternative structure.

facts.statement: Module LIBU licensing requires home-regulator prudential compliance including CRAR, LCR, NSFR and Leverage Ratio.
Module CODF mandates appointments for Controlled Functions requiring Approved Individual status, with separate criteria for Designated Functions.
facts.detail: Module GOV covers governing body appointment, remuneration, staffing and compliance; module SYSCO covers outsourcing, risk management and record-keeping.

facts.statement: Module ACBU lists xxviii+ permitted IBU activities including loan participation/MRPA, OTC derivatives, letter-of-credit negotiation, capital-market product distribution and payment services; effecting insurance contracts is prohibited.

Under module BIFC all IBU transactions must be in specified foreign currency via bank transfers, an INR SNRRA account is permitted for administrative expenses, and IBUs may lend INR-denominated loans to residents and non-residents subject to FEMA.
Module CLIC classifies clients into Retail, Professional and Market Counterparty categories with reclassification rules.

Module KICA makes a Key Information document and Client Agreement mandatory; module OEOH imposes best-execution obligations with voice/electronic communication recording and direct electronic access rules; module COIN governs conflicts of interest; modules TRUST and CHDR cover trust/custody services and complaints/dispute resolution.

Module PRBB sets 9 prudential principles: Capital Adequacy, Credit Risk, Related Parties, Concentration Risk, Market Risk, Operational Risk, IRRBB, Liquidity Risk and Group Risk; capital is held at parent-bank level per home regulations under Basel III.
facts.detail: Module LQRS covers liquidity ratios, funding strategy, stress testing and independent oversight; module PRDS covers reporting/disclosures with breach notification for CRAR, LCR, NSFR and Leverage Ratio breaches.

facts.statement: April-2024 Banking Handbook amendments: the FATF-specific jurisdiction test for Representative Office and GAO opening was replaced by 'track record in AML/CFT compliance in home jurisdiction'; ODIs were clarified as Qualified Financial Contracts under the Bilateral Netting Act, 2020; and electronic trading platform section TPVB 3.v was deleted.

For foreign bank IBUs the Section 19(2) shareholding restriction is exempted for shares held as security or received in debt satisfaction (which must be disposed within 5 years), and the Section 20(1) lending restriction does not apply.
IBUs require minimum capital of USD 20 million, are exempt from CRR and SLR requirements, and term deposits of USD 500,000 or more are classified as bulk deposits.
Regional Rural Bank ownership is split Centre 50%, Sponsor Bank 35% and State Government 15%; public sector banks hold about 60% of banking assets.

RBI was established in 1935 with headquarters in Mumbai; the MPC targets CPI inflation of 4% +/- 2%; gross NPAs fell from above 9% (2018) to below 3% (2025); Ways and Means Advances are repaid within 3 months.
Key development finance institutions: NABARD (1982, Mumbai), SIDBI (1990, Lucknow), EXIM Bank (1982, Mumbai), NHB (1988, New Delhi) and NaBFID (2021, Mumbai, with private capital up to 49%).
facts.detail: Payments banks have a deposit limit of Rs 2 lakh; neo-banks operate without their own licence; PMJDY has over 50 crore accounts.

facts.statement: E-wallets in IFSC cannot hold INR or crypto/stablecoins; NABARD refinance goes to the rural sector and the RBI regulates commercial paper issuance.
facts.detail: Cross-confirmed by PYQ: NABARD refinances the rural sector; RBI issues CP guidelines.
